subject: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Kim Choi <kim.choi@brightline.ai>, Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)

Thanks team — follow up from our handoff call. Per the onboarding plan we discussed, we're ready to run a controlled throughput/latency validation so we can sign off the performance acceptance gate. Summary of the targets we agreed to: 

- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s (steady-state, 10 minute window)
- P95 tail latency: < 300 ms for prompt sizes <= 512 tokens
- 99th percentile: expect < 800 ms (not a hard block, but we want visibility)

What we need from Brightline for the run:
1) Execute the attached load script (brightline-loadscript-v1.yml) against the staging API endpoint and include a 5-minute warmup before measurement.
2) Collect per-request telemetry columns: request_id, start_ts, end_ts, model_version, prompt_tokens, latency_ms, error_code, span_id. If you can't provide span_id, include a consistent session_id.
3) Share raw CSV results (example columns above) and a short summary (sustained RPS, p50/p95/p99).

Attachments: brightline-loadscript-v1.yml (run script template). We can accept results in CSV or the Redwood perf packet (see attached perf-evidence-packet.pdf for the fields we need).

Proposed dates: do a dry-run on Mon 6 Dec then a measurement run on Wed 8 Dec. If that works for you, please confirm and include any questions about warmup, KV cache behavior, or tokenization differences.

Next step: if the run meets the targets we'll capture the artifacts and mark the Performance Acceptance milestone complete in the onboarding checklist (HUBSPOT-RECORD-4729).

Thanks — Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
From: Kim Choi <kim.choi@brightline.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline SRE <sre@brightline.ai>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)

Thanks Neha — we can run the dry-run today. A couple quick clarifications before we start: 

- For warmup, is 5 minutes of continuous traffic sufficient or do you want a progressive ramp? We typically do a 3-step ramp (25%/60%/100%).
- Our deployment uses a tokenization step that is outside Redwood's runtime (pre-tokenizer microservice). Do you want us to include that latency in the per-request latency column or provide it separately?

I've attached our initial dry-run export (run_results_20261206.csv) so you can get a sense of distribution. Quick read: sustained RPS ~110 for 5 minutes, p95 ~320ms, p99 ~560ms — looks promising but will run the full script tomorrow.

Attachment: run_results_20261206.csv

— Kim
Principal SRE, Brightline AI
kim.choi@brightline.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Kim Choi <kim.choi@brightline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)

Kim — thanks for the dry-run and the CSV. A few quick notes after a first pass: 

- Ramp: the 3-step ramp is fine. Please include a 5-minute steady-state measurement after you reach 100% for the primary metric window.
- Tokenization: please provide tokenization latency as a separate column if the step is outside Redwood runtime. We'll combine it in a follow-up analysis but prefer to see both so we can isolate where tail spikes originate.
- Warm cache: please run a 60s prefix-only warmup at the start of the warm period so the KV cache populates. Indicate in the CSV the timestamp when warmup ends (column: warmup_end_ts).

Upload the raw CSVs to the shared folder: https://drive.redwood.company/shared/brightline/onboard-telemetry and paste the Drive link in the reply. We'll ingest the CSV into our perf pipeline and run the Redwood comparison scripts.

Also: Ben and Laura — cc'ing you for visibility. Ben, we may ask you to run the quick CSV->telemetry conversion script if the column names don't match our template (I flagged run_results_20261206 for one missing span_id).

If the Wed run looks like the dry-run, we'll schedule a 30-minute readout on Thu for sign-off.

Best,
Neha

--
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Kim Choi <kim.choi@brightline.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)

Quick note from the platform side: thanks for the CSV, Kim. If you need, I can run a small helper to normalize the CSV to our perf template — main fields we absolutely need: request_id, start_ts (ISO), end_ts (ISO), latency_ms, model_version, prompt_tokens, error_code, span_id/session_id. 

If span_id is missing, include a stable session_id per host instance; that'll let us cluster by origin. I'll drop the helper script into the shared Drive folder under /tools and ping when it's uploaded. Also, if you see tail spikes around just after warmup, include a marker — we've seen tokenization GC and remote cache misses cause that pattern.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Kim Choi <kim.choi@brightline.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook + throughput/latency run request (Brightline)

Following up with the measurement run we completed this morning (attached run_results_20261209.csv). Summary: 

- Sustained RPS (10m window): 115 req/s (target 120 req/s)
- P50: 95 ms | P95: 280 ms | P99: 510 ms
- Observed a set of 2 short spike windows (~30s total) where p99 jumped to ~1.1s. Those coincide with increased tokenization latency on our pre-tokenizer microservice.
- Error rate: 0.3% (mostly 504s from our tokenization service when it was under load)

Attachments: run_results_20261209.csv, perf-evidence-packet.pdf

Next steps we'd like to propose:
1) Joint investigation on tokenization pipeline (we think trimming or batching pre-tokenizer calls will reduce tail spikes).
2) Repeat a tuned run once tokenization is addressed — target 120 req/s steady-state.
3) 30-minute readout with Redwood engineering to validate artifacts and close this gate.

We can do the readout Fri 10 Dec 10:00 PST or Mon 13 Dec 09:00 PST — which works for you?

Thanks — Kim
Principal SRE, Brightline AI
